news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal legend considered international retirement after 2026 World Cup - but is still targeting 1,000 goals
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo considered retiring from international football after the World Cup before deciding to extend his Portugal career. Ronaldo - who turns 42 in February - will win his 234th cap against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday, with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus confirming that the former Manchester United and Real Madrid will start the Nations League fixture. Some commentators have suggested the game at the Jose Alvalade Stadium - the home of Ronaldo's first club Sporting - could be his international farewell, but the five-time Ballon d'Or winner said he will finish when "I feel like I'm not doing anything here". news.title: Harry Kane says England’s World Cup exit ‘hurt more than any other’
news.lede: ‘It wasn’t the team that we wanted and said we’d be’. England host Spain in Nations League on Saturday. Harry Kane has described England’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina as his most painful tournament exit because of how the team lost sight of who they were. The captain is determined to move on as quickly as possible and is chasing a statement performance against Spain at Wembley on Saturday night in the Nations League.

news.title: Harry Kane opens up on true impact of England's World Cup heartbreak vs Argentina
news.lede: Harry Kane insists England must put the “hurt” of the last World Cup behind them. Kane admits the pain of losing to Argentina last summer was even worse for him personally than missing the penalty against France in the 2022 quarter final. Three Lions captain Kane admitted they did not show their “true selves” against Argentina in the semi-final but says they must use that as motivation in the future. England start their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday and Kane wants to start a new chapter after the pain in the United States.

news.title: De Laurentiis wanted to 'shoot' Infantino, then applauded his World Cup show
news.lede: ROME, Sept 23 - Napoli President Aurelio De Laurentiis has a gift for turning football politics into cinema, and FIFA President Gianni Infantino found himself cast as both villain and hero in the Italian film producer's latest monologue on the state of the game. Speaking after receiving a lifetime achievement award from Italy's Foreign Press Association on Wednesday, De Laurentiis stopped short of directly attacking Infantino, who has faced calls to resign after exploring a plan under which private investors would have bought shares in the World Cup and other competitions. Instead, the Napoli owner offered a barbed assessment of the FIFA chief's rise and global profile before admitting he had been impressed by the staging of this year's World Cup. "Infantino is someone who does his job from his point of view," De Laurentiis said during the ceremony in Rome.

news.title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner
news.lede: England beat Spain 5-1 in the final of the Transplant World Cup in Frankfurt. When Martyn Jackson walked off the pitch after Ramsbottom United's 2-1 win over Cheadle Town in October 2024, it never crossed his mind that one day he could be a World Cup winner. In fact, in the days after that match, his goal was just staying alive. Just a couple of days after the final whistle, Jackson started to feel unwell during the night.

(Photo by PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA / AFP) England begins its Nations League campaign against world champions Spain at Wembley on September 26 just nine weeks after its painful last-four World Cup loss to Argentina in Atlanta. London Bukayo Saka believes the England squad still has a “scar in us” following its agonising World Cup semifinal defeat. England begins its Nations League campaign against world champions Spain at Wembley on September 26 just nine weeks after it conceded two late goals in a painful last-four loss to Lionel Messi’s Argentina in Atlanta.

news.title: Virgil van Dijk hits back at ‘nonsense’ claims that he influenced Netherlands’ World Cup tactics
news.lede: Virgil van Dijk has strongly rejected accusations that he dictated former head coach Ronald Koeman’s tactical setup during the Netherlands’ World Cup campaign, branding the allegations "completely baseless". Addressing Dutch reporters in a tense press conference, the Liverpool captain and national team skipper called suggestions that he drove tactical changes prior to their last-16 elimination by Morocco "utter nonsense". Directing his response to a journalist, Van Dijk said: "One of your colleagues also said, of course, that it was my idea to switch to playing with a back five. He added: "The fact is we simply failed at the World Cup; those are the hard facts.
